spoken_words: Hey, why'd you eat them? I thought you were a vegetarian.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I didn't. I just wanted to leave.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: More tea, Edna?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: What kind of little boy has a tea set?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Huh. I think we both know the answer to that... a lucky boy.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: You know, Seymour, there's an innocence about you that can be quite charming.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Oh? Well, I've always admired your tart honesty and ability to be personally offended by broad social trends.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Really?...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mmm-hmm. Very much. And your laugh...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: You mean "ha"?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mmm-hmm. That's the one that makes me feel... H... H... Hoo, boy. You, ah, have a breath mint I could borrow?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: I've got some menthol cigarettes.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Oh, the heck with it!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mmmmm.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: You are never going to guess what I saw at Martin's party after you guys left! You know that playhouse? Well, I...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Good gravy!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: So I looked in the window and there it was, the grossest sight I have ever...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Bart Simpson, report to the Principal's Office immediately!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Now, Bart... son... I don't know what you think you saw, but, uh, let me assure you...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: What Seymour... Oh... What Principal Skinner means to say, Bart, is that sometimes a little boy's imagination can run away with him.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: That's the best you can do? You could've at least said you were giving her CPR or rehearsing a play.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Is it too late to say that?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: We're just a little concerned. If people were to find out the principal was dating a teacher, they might see it as a conflict of interest.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: And there are those who might try to use it against us for their own advantage.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Like me for one.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Like you for... Bart, if life has taught me one lesson repeatedly, it's to know when I'm beaten. Let's talk deal.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: As you know, Bart, your permanent record will one day disqualify you from all but the hottest and noisiest jobs.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: What do you say, son? You keep our secret and some other student can inherit your gloomy, windblown future.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Deal.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: This is a great day for forbidden love.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mmmm. This dessert is exquisite. What do you call it?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Applesauce.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Oh, of course. I'm sorry, I... I don't get out to restaurants much.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: That's okay, I don't entertain much. Usually it's just soup for one, salad for one, wine for three...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: You know, I always thought I'd fall for a woman just like Mother... even though I didn't want to. And now that I haven't, I've discovered what true happiness can be, Edna.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Seymour, swallow that applesauce and kiss me.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I'm afraid I already swallowed it while you were talking.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mmm... / Oh... / / ETC.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Good morning, students. Way to go there, Wendell. There's Ralph -- he knows the score. Jimbo, how's that hat today? Janey, Janey, bo-faney!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: "The only way to survive a deadly blaze is..." Oh heck, life is too short for fire safety. Let's go outside and pick wildflowers.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Bart Simpson to the Principal's Office. Post haste.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Bart, so good to see you! I have a little favor to ask you.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I'd like you to give this note to Edna when you get back to class. I don't think I have to tell you it's for her eyes only.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I hear reading...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Do you think anyone saw us?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: No. It went just as we planned, except they confiscated my thermos of cola at the door.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Oh.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Skinner. Krabappel. What are you two doing here?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Superintendent Chalmers!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Uh, why, we're... We're, uh, on a... a, uh Uh, uh, what do you call... uh, field trip.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Uh, with a student.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Yes! He's, uh...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: He's, uh, he's... purchasing refreshments in the lobby.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I'll... I'll... I'll go get him right now. Car keys, car keys, car keys.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Stop pushing me. What's going on?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Just enjoy the movie. It has Tom Berenger.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Do you think they actually filmed this in Atlanta?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: I don't know. I don't think it's important.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Yeah.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mother doesn't approve of me dating, so I need you to keep her busy for a few hours while Edna and I sneak out.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, I can't take much more of this.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: You wouldn't happen to have any real cakes around here, would you?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, can't I just turn the page for you?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Okay. That one.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Ow!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Bart Simpson! How many times do I have to tell you, no talking! Report to the principal's office!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: But... But I wasn't...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: And here, take this with you.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mrs. Krabappel, Bart has something he wants to say to you.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: I won't say it!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Bart!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh... I love you, Edna Krabappel.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Nelson Muntz
spoken_words: Where are you registered, Simpson?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Thank you, Bart. That was very sweet. You may sit down now.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: They're not going to get away with this.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: I'm going to step out for a few minutes, class. Martin, you're in charge.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, now Martin's scoring off of me. Oh, that is it. Listen up, everybody! Follow me!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Okay crew, set your faces to stunned.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Um... Um.. School dismissed.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Milhouse Van Houten
spoken_words: ...And then Bart opened the door and Principal Skinner and Mrs. Krabappel were kissing... and swearing!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Wow!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I was in the library at the time, but Janey told me that Principal Skinner and Bart's teacher, Mrs.... What's her name?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Krabappel?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Yeah, Krabappel. They were naked in the closet together.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, my goodness.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Wait a minute. Bart's teacher's name is "Krabappel?" I've been calling her "Crandall." Why didn't someone tell me? Oh, I've been making an idiot out of myself.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: The baby looked at you? Sara, get me Superintendent Chalmers.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: Thank you, Sara.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Skin-ner!!!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Superintendent Chalmers!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: The whole town's in an uproar about your sleazy shenanigans! Now I'm going to give you a choice. You can give up this tawdry, fulfilling relationship, or you two will be out of here so fast your mortarboards will spin. And where is your mortarboard, anyway?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Uh, right here, sir!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: So what'll it be, Seymour?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Well... I'm sorry, but, ah, I can't give up the woman I love.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Well then, I'm afraid you leave me no choice. I want you out of the building by three o'clock. You're fired. Edna, too.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Well, it's going to be hard to say good-bye to all of you. We've had a lot of fun together.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Nelson, Nelson, Nelson. Oh, how many kids have you beaten up this year?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Nelson Muntz
spoken_words: I 'unno. Fifty.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Ah, fifty... Where does the time go?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: You, you, uh, wanted to see me, Principal Skinner?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mmm-hmm, it's Mr. Skinner now. I'm just a man. Bart, I want to apologize for the awkward position Edna and I put you in. Your... your help made our love possible. I don't know what we'll do without you. Well, so long.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Wait a second. You don't have to leave just because Superintendent Chalmers told you to.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: What are you getting at?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: You've spent your whole life following orders -- from your mother, the army, Superintendent Chalmers. Just this once, man, stand up for yourself.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Okay, Bart.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Let's go, Seymour.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Okay, Edna.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I... No, wait! We're not going anywhere. I'm going to do what Bart should have told me to do a long time ago!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Attention, Springfield. We have barricaded ourselves in the school and are not coming down until our demands are met.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Groundskeeper Willie
spoken_words: Willie hears ya, Willie don't care.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Obviously, you two have no experience causing a scene.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Kent Brockman
spoken_words: I'll be right there.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Kent Brockman
spoken_words: Alright, people! We've got an escaped octopus on the roof of Springfield Elementary! Let's roll! Two cameras!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Kent Brockman
spoken_words: ...and so once again, I've been had. But an even more interesting story has developed high atop this two story school. A love story...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Skinner!! Get off of my school!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: No! You get off of my school!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Homer, Bart's up there!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Give me that! Bart, this is your father. Do you know where the remote is? I looked all over the house.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Did you check your pocket?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: It was in... It was in my pocket.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: Fine. Stay in the school. We don't want you to come out.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: You got it!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: Damn. All right, boys, roll up the sound truck. We'll blast 'em out with music.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Oh, Edna, I hope this siege never ends.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Seymour, you're heaven in Hush Puppies.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Turn the music off!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: Heh, it's working like a charm, boys! Now cut the power and hit 'em with the lights!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I'll get it. Talk to me.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: You have got to end this thing, Seymour.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: We're not coming down until our jobs are reinstated and you acknowledge and celebrate our love.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: No one would like to celebrate your love more than I, but I am a public servant and not permitted to use my own judgment in any way.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Then let us take our case directly to the townspeople!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Oh yeah, that'll be real productive. Who do you wanna talk to first? The guy in the bumblebee suit or the one with the bone through his hair?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Yeah, all right. Just come on down.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Well, this is it.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: What are you going to do?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I'm going to go out there, and tell every man, woman and child that I love Edna Krabappel.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Well, that's nice. But first, you've gotta grab their attention. And I think I know how...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: I... have a bomb.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: Hey, wait a minute. Those are hot dogs. Armour Hot dogs.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: What kind of man wears Armour Hot Dogs?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: It was a good idea, Bart. But it's just not working.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Just speak from the heart, Seymour. Tell them how we brought a little happiness into each other's lives. Ask them why they're forcing two dedicated people to choose between their careers and their hearts...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Krusty the Clown
spoken_words: "Sex Cauldron?" I thought they closed that place down.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: What are you people talking about?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Dr. Julius Hibbert
spoken_words: My child told me you two were having sex in the school janitor's closet.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: You know, "making babies"?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: This is absurd. I did not have relations in that closet. And the fact is, I haven't... ...uh...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Yes?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Seymour, I think you'd better tell them. It's the only way to clear our names.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Well, everyone, the fact is: I haven't ever had relations. I am a virgin.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Nelson Muntz
spoken_words: Haw haw!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Hey, does this mean that Mrs. Krabappel is a virgin, too?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Ha!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Well, Seymour, it's clear you've been falsely accused, because no one... anywhere... ever... would pretend to be a forty-four-year-old virgin.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Krusty the Clown
spoken_words: Oh, that's for sure!

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Dr. Julius Hibbert
spoken_words: I'm inclined to agree.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Groundskeeper Willie
spoken_words: Ach. I'll never look at him the same again.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Lenny Leonard
spoken_words: That was more than I wanted to know.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Okay, well, um, Edna, Seymour... in light of these, er, er, revelations, I, uh, suppose we, uh, overreacted.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Do we have our jobs back?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: What? Oh, yes, yes, yes. Sure. Just, um, you know, keep the lewdness to a minimum.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: I'm outta here. Skinny, Krabby, catch ya later.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Uh -- Hold on, Bart. May we have a word with you?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: We want to thank you for helping us through a difficult period.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, no problemo. So, I guess now you'll be getting married or something, huh?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Well, actually, Seymour and I have decided to break up.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Huh?

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: We can't continue on like this, trying to build a private relationship in public -- the whole town watching our every move with a fine-tooth comb.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Mm-hmm. I'm used to humiliation, but not in front of a crowd that size.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: No.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Aw, but you seemed like such a good couple.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Bart, when you get a little older, you're going to learn that sometimes romances don't turn out exactly the way you'd like them to...

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: That's why I love elementary school, Edna. The children believe anything you tell them.

title: Grade School Confidential
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Whoo!... Oh, Seymour...!

spoken_words: Marge, mail's here.

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: Bills... bills... oo, a free sample of gasoline... a note from Publishers' Clearinghouse saying we're out of the running... oh look, Lisa! You got something.

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: Oh, Foreign Language Institute. Oh, my German verb wheel!

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: When? When? Ich bin hungrig!

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: Homer, this is yours.

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: Yes! My precious "CarTOONS!" "Who pumped Ethyl?!"

name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, how come I never get any mail?

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: I'm sorry, honey. Here, you can have the junk mail.

title: The Canine Mutiny

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Wow, my own credit card! Thanks, "Santos!"

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: A quarter?! Well, you're just the dog that keeps on giving, aren'cha?

name: Bart Simpson

spoken_words: ... and "Zebra Girl," and "Zillionaire," and "Zoidzilla."

name: Comic Book Guy

spoken_words: And will there be any more splurging today?

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson
raw_location_text: The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop
spoken_words: Oh my, yes. Hmm, I'll take that hardbound Radioactive Man collection.

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Comic Book Guy
raw_location_text: The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop
spoken_words: Ah, a superb choice: in volume two, Radioactive Man travels through time to defeat Jesse Owens at the 1936 Olympic Games.

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson
raw_location_text: The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop
spoken_words: Put it all on my credit card, my good man.

raw_location_text: The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop
spoken_words: Ooh, pardon me, "Santos" -- if that is your real name, Bart Simpson -- but your phony credit is no good here. Now make like my pants and split.

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, what good's a credit card if you can't even use it?

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: "Order by phone. 1-800 --" Our phone doesn't go up to eight hundred. Unless...

spoken_words: Mom, this is for you: 15 pounds of

title: The Canine Mutiny

spoken_words: Vancouver smoked salmon. Here. Smell it!

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, Bart, you didn't have to do that. Oh!

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: And for Homer --

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Wow! A golf shirt! With my corporate logo on it!

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, it smells like salmon, too! Thanks, boy!

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: And for the college-bound... 500 stay-alert capsules.

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Wow, "Trucker's Choice." That is so sweet.

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Bart, where did you get all this stuff?

title: The Canine Mutiny
name: Bart Simpson

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lenny Leonard
spoken_words: Uhhh, attention everybody. Work harder. Bye!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, but Daddy doesn't feel so good.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Waylon Smithers
spoken_words: Well, sir, I have to get to work. Lenny's a real bear on tardiness.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Are there any chores I can do?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Waylon Smithers
spoken_words: Uh, no, no. You just stay here and maintain your dignity.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Ah, here's a chance to earn my keep. I will go out and get these items from the food jobber.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Grocery store, please!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I am riding on a bus.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh my, no! I'm Monty Burns!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I'm shopping.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh my... I wonder which is the cereal for me...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Uh, oh, excuse me, can you tell me where I might find the "Burns-O's"?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Krusty the Clown
spoken_words: Sorry, Pops. They don't put nobodies on cereal boxes.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Hmm. Well, I suppose this one looks a bit like me...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, thank you, Shoppie. I... I ventured in to search for milk when the door snapped shut behind me.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Ketchup, catsup... ketchup, catsup... ketchup, catsup... Ugh. I'm in way over my head.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Are you here to solve my ketchup problem?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Wh... where are you taking me? What's happening?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Chief Wiggum
spoken_words: Relax. You've gone off your nut, so we're stuffing you into an old folks home. Those, uh, store guys signed the commitment papers.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: But I'm shopping!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Here you go, honey. That's about all the recycling I can handle today.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Dad, if you just drink one more, I'll have a full bag.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: There's got to be more trash around here somewhere...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Hey, why don't you try the old folks home? They practically live in their own filth!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Thanks, Dad!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: You're welcome, honey.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Grampa Simpson
spoken_words: That's the activity room. We're not allowed in there. That's the library. Not allowed in there, either. And don't even think about going in the game room...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Egad, man, how are we supposed to pass the time?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Grampa Simpson
spoken_words: Best bet is to stake yourself out a good spot at the starin' window...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: So this is how the Monty Burns saga ends... If I hadn't surrounded myself with those spineless yes men...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: What do you mean you don't have anything to recycle? You must have some magazines, or newspapers.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: That voice! That shrill, disagreeable voice! It's her!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Grampa Simpson
spoken_words: Sorry, we're not allowed to read newspapers. They angry up the blood.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: You! The troublemaking girl!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: My name is Lisa, Mr. Burns. Lisa Simpson.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: It doesn't matter what your name is, you idiot! What I want to know is: will you help me get my money back?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Ha! I'd never help you. You're the worst man in the world.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Yes! That's the kind of moxie I'm looking for. You're hired!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: No, I'm not!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Waylon Smithers
spoken_words: Sir, I'm so sorry my grocer committed you. We'll never shop there again.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Not now, Smithers. I've got an empire to rebuild, and the person who's going to help me is... that girl!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Please!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: No.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Please!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: No.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Please!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Sir, we've never met before, but my name is Mr. Burns and I want your daughter to help make me rich again.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: You mean Maggie?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Ah, the baby who shot me. No, I was referring to your other daughter.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Lisa! You have a guest!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: So, um, how's life in the gutter?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: You again.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I've realized the error of my ways, Lisa. I need someone with your integrity to help me. Please don't refuse this poor old man.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Oh... if I did agree to help you, you could only earn money by doing good, socially responsible things. Nothing evil.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: "Nothing evil." That's exactly the kind of radical thinking I need! It's a deal.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: See that, boy? Why aren't you making any business deals?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: I'll do it this afternoon...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: You mean there are actually people who will pay good money for garbage?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Not good money, really. Each can'll get you a nickel.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, don't pooh-pooh a nickel, Lisa. A nickel will buy you a steak and kidney pie, a cup of coffee, a slice of cheesecake, and a newsreel! With enough change leftover to ride the trolley from Battery Park to the Polo Grounds.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: There's a can.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: You have to cut these six-pack holders up. Otherwise fish get trapped in them.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I see...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Nelson Muntz
spoken_words: Haw haw!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: My first dollar! Thanks to you, Lisa, and our hemp-smoking friend. Shine on, you crazy diamond.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Well, Lisa, as my advisor, you're entitled to ten percent.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: It's all right. I understand. But we really could have used that twelve thousand dollars.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, I'm not doing this for the money. I'm just happy knowing that future generations will enjoy unspoiled median strips and pristine highway embankments.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: There's a can.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Kent Brockman
spoken_words: And from our "It's Funny When It Happens To Them" file... Remember millionaire C. Montgomery Burns? The man who blocked out our sun, ran over a local boy, and stole Christmas from 1981 to 1985? Well, guess who's flat broke and picking up trash for a living?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Please be Flanders, please be Flanders, please be Flanders...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Kent Brockman
spoken_words: Excuse me, Mr. Burns, now that you're completely ruined, how do you feel?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Excellent. I'm on my way back to the top. I've turned these cans into "can do!"

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Kent Brockman
spoken_words: Well, you smell terrible! Good luck to you, sir.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Wow, he went from stinking rich to just plain stinking.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Good one, Mom! / You're so bad, honey.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: You guys shouldn't laugh at him. Mr. Burns has changed. He's different now.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Yeah, he's broke!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Two in a row!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, you've really turned my life around these past few weeks, Lisa. I've got my own business again, my beloved employees... oh consargnit. Eh, come on, let's pick up the pace, you neglected old nincompoops!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Mr. Burns, if you want people to do a good job, you can't bully them. You have to show them they're appreciated.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, capital idea, partner. People, if we meet this week's quota, I'll take you to the most duck-filled pond you ever sat by.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Grampa Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, hot-diggity! That's how they got me to vote for Lyndon LaRouche!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Wow, even I didn't know he was so committed to recycling! See? I told you Mr. Burns has changed. See?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Lisa, nobody likes a gloater. Right, Homie?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Uh-huh.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: See!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Yes, thank you, everyone. But -- 10% of your applause should go to my little partner, Lisa Simpson. For if it were not for her infectious moralizing, we would not be here today to witness the unveiling of... The Li'l Lisa Recycling Plant!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: Aw, ain't that cute? Makes Li'l Debbie look like a pile of puke!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Would you like to be the first to take a tour of the plant, Li'l Lisa?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I'd love to -- Partner!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: The whole plant is a environmentally-sound. It's powered by old newspapers. The machinery is made entirely of used cans. And the windows are from the old liquor bottles we collected.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I thought I told you to stop licking my windows!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I'm so proud of you, Mr. Burns! You're getting your fortune back and you're doing it without endangering the planet or cozying up to the Aspen crowd.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, hold your accolades to the end of the tour. You haven't seen the best part!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I couldn't watch your demonstration of the fish caught in the plastic rings without getting an idea. Look out over the water.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I figured if one six-pack holder will catch one fish, a million sewn together will catch a million fish. Watch.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: What's going on?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I call it the Burns Omni-Net. It sweeps the sea clean.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, dear God!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I call our product: Li'l Lisa's Patented Animal Slurry! It's a high-protein feed for farm animals, insulation for low-income housing, a powerful explosive, and a top-notch engine coolant. And best of all, it's made from 100% recycled animals!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I think I'm going to be sick...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, a spoonful of slurry will cure what ails ya!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Ach! You haven't changed at all! You're still evil! And when you're trying to be good, you're even more evil!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: I don't understand. Pigs need food, engines need coolant, dynamiters need dynamite. I'm supplying it to them, at a tidy profit, and not a single sea creature was wasted. You inspired it all, Li'l Lisa.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Stop! Don't recycle! It's murder! You're helping Mr. Burns!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: No! It's evil! Please stop recycling!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, I can't get the smell of slurry out of my clothes! I was a fool to help that horrible old man!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, I hope you learned your lesson, Lisa. Never help anyone.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Waylon Smithers
spoken_words: Simpson, what are you doing here? Why aren't you at work?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: I made a bad mistake and Lenny sent me home to think about what I did. But I don't remember what it was so I'm watching TV.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Waylon Smithers
spoken_words: Well, Lenny's reign of terror is over. Mr. Burns bought the plant back this morning, and...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Enough chit-chat. I need to see Lisa.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I don't want to talk to you, Mr. Burns.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, I think you will. You see, I've just sold the Li'l Lisa Recycling Plant for 120 million dollars!

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Congratulations...

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: C. Montgomery Burns
spoken_words: Oh, don't congratulate me, congratulate Bay State Fish Sticks... as my advisor, you're entitled to ten percent of the proceeds.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Lis, have I told you lately that I love you?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Wow! I've never seen so much money! Oh, but I can't accept that, knowing where it came from. Can I, Mom?

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Lisa, you do whatever your conscience tells you.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: You did the right thing, sweetheart.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Dr. Julius Hibbert
spoken_words: Well, that's the first case I've ever seen of a man suffering four simultaneous heart attacks.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I'm sorry, Dad.

title: The Old Man and the Lisa
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Um, Dad... ten percent of 120 million dollars isn't twelve thousand. It's...

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Turn it down! We don't wanna wake up mom and dad!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Oh my goodness. Kids! Homer! We're late for church! I'm glad I dressed last night.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, I'd love to go with you, honey, but I've got a lot of work to do around the bed.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Homer, the Lord only asks for an hour a week.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: In that case, he should've made the week an hour longer. Lousy God.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: ...and the very same goes for Ezekiel, which brings us back to our starting point, the nine tenets of constancy.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: DAMMIT!!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: I seem to have lost my place, so I'll start over.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: Aw, for the luvva crumbcake!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Our sermon today is on constancy, inasmuch as the...

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Moreover, by dint of the appreciation of these principles we can learn...the importance of constancy, sweet constancy.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Thank you, Lord, for delivering us from Reverend Lovejoy!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: / Yahoo! / Oh, man, am I glad to get outta there! / etc.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Hey, calm down. You're wrinkling your church clothes!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Who cares? This is the best part of the week!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: It's the longest possible time before more church.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Church shouldn't be a chore. It should help you in your daily life.

title: Homer's Enemy
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: "Barney Gumbel".

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: It should, but it doesn't. Now who's going with Daddy to the dump?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Me! Me!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: The dump?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Yeah. We're gonna get rid of the Christmas tree. It's starting to turn brown.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Wanna come with?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: No, no, I don't feel like going to a trash pile today.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: It's your life.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: We'll bring you back something nice.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Can you believe it? They give you five Q's and only two U's. What a world.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: It's crazy!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: So what's on your mind, Marge?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: ...sermons about "constancy" and "prudissitude" are all very well and good, but the church could be doing so much more to reach out to people.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Oh, I don't see you volunteering to make things better.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Well... okay. I will volunteer!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: I wasn't prepared for that.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: C'mon, Christmas tree.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Okay. Who's up for some scrounging?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Hey, here's a perfectly good basketball half!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I found a Malibu Stacy with no head!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh my God! Help me, Lisa!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Lisa! Dad! C'mere quick! There is something that you won't believe!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: What the heck is that?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Maybe it's a box from the future!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: It looks Japanese.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Wh... what's going on? Wh... wha... why am I on a Japanese box?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, my God, what is that?...

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Ned Flanders
spoken_words: I'm meek... but I could probably stand to be meeker.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: All done! I swept the aisles and put all the collection plates in the dishwasher. Oh, and you wouldn't believe how many dead pigeons there were in the organ.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Marge, you are a real time-saver. Do you know, thanks to you, I've rediscovered a form of shame that's gone unused for 700 years.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Wow.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Lovejoy here.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Reverend, this is Principal Skinner. I'm facing a crisis and I didn't know to whom to turn.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: All right.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Mother's gone too far. She's put cardboard over her half of the television. We rented "Man Without a Face" -- I didn't even know he had a problem. What should I do?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Well, maybe you should read your Bible.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Um, any particular passage?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Oh, it's all good.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: All right. Thanks anyway.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Reverend, I hate to say this, but it sounded like that poor man was reaching out to you. I'm not sure your advice was all that helpful.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Oh, Marge, I was once idealistic like you. It was the mid-seventies, and I was fresh out of seminary. The Sixties were long over and people were once again ready to feel bad about themselves...

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: I came to Springfield ready to roll up my sleeves and help my fellow man.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Then the calls began.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Ned Flanders
spoken_words: ...Well, I... I think I may be coveting my own wife...

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Ned Flanders
spoken_words: I think I swallowed a toothpick.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Finally, I just stopped caring. Luckily by then, it was the 80s and no one noticed.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: But you can't let a few bad experiences sour you on helping people!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: Oh, sure I can.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Rev. Timothy Lovejoy
spoken_words: You handle it.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Me?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: No, I... I... Wait, I can't... I-- Hello...?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: Uh, yeah, hi, I'm callin' for Reverend Lovejoy. Who is this?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, well, this is... um... the, uh... the Listen Lady!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: Yeah, well listen, lady. I've got so many problems, I.... I don't even know where to begin here.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Okay, uh, why don't you start from the top?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: All rightee... Uh, number one: I've lost the will to live.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, that's ridiculous, Moe. You've got lots to live for.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: Really? That's not what Reverend Lovejoy's been tellin' me. Wow, you're good. Thanks!

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: Hi, it's me again. I got another problem. Uh, this one's about my cat.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Moe Szyslak
spoken_words: Yeah, shut up. I'm asking her.

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Why would you volunteer at the church?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: I don't know... guilt?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Volunteering is for suckers! Do you know that so-called "volunteers" don't even get paid?

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Well, I think volunteering is great. Deep down it makes you feel --

title: In Marge We Trust
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Homer! Will you get that crazy box off the dinner table? It came from the dump.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Oh Mother, you are still the master of deception.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: ...So in 1966, a brave young man named Seymour Skinner enlisted and shipped out to Vietnam, where he rose to become Platoon Sergeant. Ralph?

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Sgt. Skinner was a hero. He risked capture many times behind enemy lines.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: And he survived to make it back to Springfield, where he became the fine educator we salute tonight.

title: The Principal and the Pauper

spoken_words: Now, I know the school normally serves cake only on Thursdays. And I'm also well aware that today is Friday. Nevertheless, I have a surprise for you.

title: The Principal and the Pauper

spoken_words: I hope you all brought forks and plates!

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Oh! What the -- an enjoyment buzzer?!

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: Oh, thank you. What a wonderful night to share with the people and the town that I love. I have never been happier or prouder to be Seymour Skinner.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Skinner?

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: No...No he's, he's not crazy. It's true: I'm, I'm an impostor. That man is the real Seymour Skinner.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner
spoken_words: It's true. I was in his platoon... But they said you were killed on that scouting mission!

title: The Principal and the Pauper

spoken_words: That's not a funny story.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: So what's your story, Seymour? If that is your real name.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Seymour Skinner

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Principal Skinner?

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Come on! Get to the part where you steal his identity!

name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, it's one of those stories.

name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Look, lady, you obviously have at least one son.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Hey, Armin.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Mrs. Krabappel sent me. I forged my dad's signature on my report card.

name: Bart Simpson

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Bart Simpson
spoken_words: Hey, hey, hey! Easy there, you big impostor.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Not to us you're not. I mean, how would you feel if you suddenly found out Ned Flanders was an impostor?

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: My next-door neighbor? Religious guy?

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: No I don't! What I mean is, to me you're just a stranger pretending to be something he's not.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: I'm sorry, but that's just how I feel.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Well, now I don't know... Skinner, do you know anything about being a principal?

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Good enough. Armin Tamzarian's reign of terror is over. Now let us welcome our new Principal Skinner: Principal Seymour Skinner. Ah, him.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: No, please! I don't care what you've done. You're still a decent, honorable man.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Edna Krabappel-Flanders
spoken_words: Oh!

spoken_words: Now to recap our top story in its entirety: The adaptable citizens of Springfield have opened their hearts to Principal Seymour Skinner. Who...

spoken_words: Not that one. Idiots.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: I admit Sgt. Skinner seems okay... but Mr. Tamzarian pulled himself up from the streets and earned our respect and admiration.

spoken_words: Now hold on. Armin Tamzarian is an unsavory character who played us all for chumps.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: All right, all right. So, he's a fraud. I don't care! His mom doesn't care! Do any of you care?

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Gary Chalmers
spoken_words: Well, I don't see any way out of this.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Now, if you'll allow me, I think I have a solution that'll satisfy the town and let Sgt. Skinner keep his dignity.

title: The Principal and the Pauper
name: Homer Simpson

title: The Principal and the Pauper

spoken_words: Oh no we don't! Judge Snyder?

spoken_words: "This is just a note to say, I think about you every day. And when I get you all alone..." Well, it gets a little bit personal, here.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: I understand. Yoink. Wow...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: I know.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Whoa...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Tell me about it.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Oh, here's one from my mother.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Ooo, let's see what she wrote!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, you hate lotus flowers, too? Oh, don't get me started on Lotus flowers.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: No, no. It is the sign that it is time for my arranged marriage!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh. Well, congratulations.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: No, no, no. Don't you know what it means?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Not... really...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: It all happened shortly after my eighth birthday...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: O-kay, here we go...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Oh, I cannot get married. I'm just beginning to enjoy my bachelorhood. Ah, what am I going to do?!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Tell her the truth. You're not ready to get married.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: No, no, no, no, you do not know Mother. She will never quit until I am married.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Then just tell her you're already married.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: No, no. I cannot lie to my mother.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Then get married. What the hell do you want from me?!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Yes, that is right, mother. I already got married... Why did not I bother to tell you? Well, uh, the reason is...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Well, I guess I... I didn't-think-you'd-understand. Oh, got-to-go. Bye-bye-bye. I love-you. Love-you.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: It worked! It worked! The lie has set me free!!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Loser. Loser. Loser. Five... hundred.... dollars! Apu wake up! I want to buy a Yodel and this lottery ticket.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: I have this much.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: I am sorry, you do not have enough for both.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh... Oh... Ooo... Oh... Yodel.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Late night, huh?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: I'm not the type to kiss and tell, sir, but listen to this...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: You dog.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: It is my mother!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Oh, no! Oh, no! What am I going to do?!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: What's the big problem?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Bu... Don't you see?! She is here to meet my wife.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: The wife that I told her I had. I do not have a wife.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Then maybe you shouldn't of told her you did.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Oh, she's going to be here any second!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Oh, yes, that'll buy me some time. Homer, you've got to help me!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Okay... seems to me , what you oughta do is, um...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: What?! What?! What?! What?! What?!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Wellll, you could always move into my house, and tell your mom that Marge is your wife.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Is it me, or do your plans always involve some horrible web of lies?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: It's you.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Welcome to the Kwik-E-Mart. May I help... Mother! What are you doing here?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: And meet her you shall. It is a very reasonable request that can easily be granted in a timely and efficient...

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: And go we shall, because it is in the going that we at-tat-tat-tat-tat!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, that Yodel was so good. I wish I was eatin' it right now.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, crap, I forgot!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Marge, I need a small favor. For the next few days, will you pretend to be Apu's wife?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: What?!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Please? It's just for as long as his mother's living here.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: What?!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Honey, I am in my home.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: How was your day, sweetheart?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Can you feel the love?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Mother, I would like for you to meet my darling wife of many, many good years, Mmmarge.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Hello. So... What brings you to America?

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

spoken_words: Ohhhh. Here I am!

name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: Okay, gotta run. Apu, I'm sure you wanna to get upstairs and fix that broken toilet before Marge yells at you again.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

spoken_words: I'm just so honored to have you here in our home.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

spoken_words: Ach, Mother, come on, you know that one out of every 25 arranged marriages ends in divorce. Heh.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Marge Simpson
spoken_words: Oh, Bart and Lisa! You remember your father, Apu. Well, this is your father, Apu's mother.

name: Lisa Simpson
spoken_words: Ohhhh. / Hiiiii.

name: Homer Simpson
spoken_words: But you can't leave! We're scammin' an old lady at my house and I need a place to hide out.

name: Homer Simpson

spoken_words: Yeah!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

spoken_words: Well, I'm glad you were having fun, because I've had my hands full with Apu's mother.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
name: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon
spoken_words: Oh, my God!

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

spoken_words: Oh Apu, give it up.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons

spoken_words: Lied to his mother.

title: The Two Mrs. Nahasapeemapetilons
